UserAccount.title: UserAccount
UserAccount.description: Represents a user account for the RAFA Project Launcher.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user account.

createdAt.description: Timestamp indicating when the user account was created.

GameRequest.title: GameRequest
GameRequest.description: Represents a user's request for a game to be added to the RAFA Project Launcher.

id.description: Unique identifier for the game request.

gameName.description: The name of the game being requested.

platform.description: The platform for which the game is being requested (e.g., PC, PS4/5, Xbox, Switch).

notes.description: Any additional notes or comments from the user regarding the game request.

requestDate.description: The date and time when the game request was submitted.

AvailableGame.title: AvailableGame
AvailableGame.description: Represents a game that is available on the RAFA Project Launcher.

id.description: Unique identifier for the available game.

name.description: The name of the available game.

supportedPlatforms.description: A list of platforms on which the game is supported.

imageUrl.description: URL of the image for the available game.

params.name: userAccountId

definition.description: Stores game requests submitted by users. Includes the denormalized 'userAccountId' field for authorization independence.

params.name: userAccountId
params.description: The unique identifier for the user account that submitted the request.

params.name: gameRequestId
params.description: The unique identifier for the game request.

definition.description: Stores information about available games on the RAFA Project Launcher.

params.name: availableGameId
params.description: The unique identifier for the available game.

firestore.reasoning: The Firestore structure is designed to support the RAFA Project Launcher application, focusing on user accounts, game requests, and available games. It leverages path-based ownership for user-specific data (game requests) and a dedicated collection for globally available games. User accounts are stored in a top-level collection for easy authentication and management. To ensure authorization independence, the `GameRequest` documents under `/users/{userAccountId}/game_requests/{gameRequestId}` include the `userAccountId` field, enabling secure rules without needing to perform `get()` operations on parent documents. This structure facilitates QAPs by segregating user-specific data and global data into separate collections with distinct security profiles.
